result.summary: Mechanically adds explicit `#include <util/check.h>` and removes `#include <cassert>` across benchmark, fuzz, and unit test files invoking `assert` or `Assert`. A second scripted-diff commit reformats and sorts the updated include blocks using clang-format.
result.problem: Test files rely on transitive includes or `<cassert>`, creating confusion over whether `NDEBUG` could disable assertions and causing compile failures in tests when compiling without assertions in `util/check.h`. Missing direct headers also impedes running Include-What-You-Use (IWYU) analysis.
evidence: Commit 405cde959f: "The project has a compile error when compiled without assertions in util/check.h. Thus, util/check.h should be included for all assertions."
PR description: "Avoid that confusion in test code with a scripted replacement to add the util/check.h include. The changes here will also make it easier to run IWYU."
result.scope_notes: Fully mechanical scripted diff modifying includes across 153 test, bench, and fuzz files, verified with git scripts embedded in the commit messages.
result.changed_since_previous: Dropped changes to the scripted-diff lint runner tooling; the PR now consists purely of test include updates and clang-format sorting.
result.card: Adds explicit util/check.h includes and removes cassert across 153 test, benchmark, and fuzz files via scripted diffs. This avoids confusion over whether assertions can be compiled out via NDEBUG, prevents build failures when compiling with alternative check.h configurations, and facilitates IWYU tooling. The change is entirely mechanical and restricted to test code.

risk.why: Mistakes in includes would only cause test build failures caught during compilation.
